minutes.headline: Planning Board granted a site plan waiver and reduced a subdivision bond; Whalom overlay density rules stayed unsettled.
minutes.summary: A resident asked the board to ease the freestanding sign process. The board granted a site plan waiver for a dealer's license use and voted on reducing the Stone Farm bond. Most of the meeting went to how to read the Whalom overlay density rules for 274 Prospect Street, a concept presentation of an over-55 development, and a read-through of draft zoning bylaw rewrite language.

what_happened.line: The Planning Board voted to reduce the Stone Farm subdivision bond, releasing the balance and holding back the engineer's estimate for punch list work.
The board granted a site plan waiver as requested for a dealer's license use.
Most of the meeting went to reading the Whalom overlay density rules, and the board will ask the zoning officer whether relief from the ten-acre requirement can come through the Zoning Board.
A resident asked the board to ease the freestanding sign process; the request goes on the January 22nd workshop agenda with input from the building inspector.
The board continued its read-through of the draft zoning bylaw rewrite, and the director will write a memo saying the board is split on the Prospect and Cross Street parcel.

why_it_matters: A bond is the money a town holds to make sure a developer finishes roads and repairs, so cutting it to the engineer's estimate leaves less in hand if the work costs more than estimated.
The Whalom overlay density reading and the zoning rewrite set how much housing can be built on nearby parcels, and the rewrite is likely to come to Town Meeting as a vote.
watch_next: January 22nd Planning Board workshop, where the sign bylaw request is to be taken up.
The zoning officer's answer on whether the Zoning Board can grant relief from the ten-acre requirement.
